correctness.rationale: The universal line section has constant length m and is flat over the dual plane. Plane quadrics give all sections of L and their restrictions to a line span all quadratics there; restriction to its length-m divisor has zero kernel on those quadratics for m>=4. The support divisor recovers the line and then the kernel determines the constant direction. Thus the proper parameter image is closed, irreducible and three-dimensional. After splitting the quotient direction, the Quot kernel is L(-D) plus L. At rank exactly 3, the minors linearize to the map from the evaluation kernel H^0(L(-D) plus L) into the cokernel. The two Hom multipliers must send span(1,t) and span(1,t,t^2), respectively, into span(1,t,t^2) modulo the degree-m line-section polynomial. Testing 1 and t forces the first multiplier to have degree at most 1 and the second to have degree at most 1; testing t^2 for the second reduces that to degree 0. Every degree-3 obstruction in these tests is strictly below m, including m=4. The tangent dimension 3 equals local dimension, so the image is a component and is smooth at its transverse points. The family projects isomorphically onto its support divisors, hence is nondefective; over distinct projections the Hilbert and Quot descriptions identify locally as unordered sets of base points and directions with the same evaluation map. At m=3 the bound is automatic and the ambient Quot dimension is 6. The source checker was inspected, not executed: its rational row construction checks only a finite model of the exact multiplier computation, which was proved directly here.

value.rationale: An explicit regular component for the complete linear system, on every smooth plane curve of the specified degree and with a sharp small-degree boundary, is useful for understanding special secant loci of scrolls and for testing possible dimension bounds.
